audit.title: Beta Scope

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Declarative headings double as liftable claims (e.g., "Self-deployed contracts are not visible in the platform"), and each section leads with a self-contained statement. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 7 clean H2 sections, 0 level skips, no section over 238 words. The one gap: 0 tables — a limitations page is the canonical case for a scannable summary matrix.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Good. Hard numbers land ("Ten addresses per evaluation", single-use permits, ERC-20/ERC-3643, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Weak points: 0 numerals carry units, no version strings, and vague quantifiers "some"/"most" appear.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Good. Inline links to ISO 3166-1, CRE Service Quotas, and the CRE Connect SDK on GitHub; mostly internal cross-links to canonical concept pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. Crisp statements like "Data Validators are a curated catalog maintained by Chainlink" and the two-signing-model definition are verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`, no og/twitter tags. A visible "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" exists in body but is not machine-exposed in `<head>`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Neutral. 0 code blocks; largely acceptable for a scope page, though a minimal snippet for the `wallet_risk_scoring` policy config would help agents.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good. Covers what's excluded in Beta and why, but lacks symptom-phrased entry points ("why isn't my contract showing in the platform", "can I use ACE with a DEX/vault").

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Consistent entity naming (ACE Platform, Coordinator API, CRE). Minor grammar slip: "no personally identifiable information (PII) are used."

audit.summary: This page enumerates the scope and limitations of the Chainlink ACE Beta, and it is well-built for extraction: declarative headings ("Signing model is chosen at onboarding") that state the answer in the heading itself, tight 78-word median sections, and useful hard limits ("Ten addresses per evaluation"). Its single biggest strength is answer-first section design; its single biggest opportunity is machine-readability — no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no `<head>` freshness signals were served, leaving agents to infer trust from prose alone. The honest verdict: strong content structure held back by absent structured metadata and a missing symptom-phrased query layer.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased headings/subheadings for the highest-traffic questions
recommendations.where: "No custom extractors or mappers" and "Self-deployed contracts are not visible in the platform"
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled sections miss how devs actually query the failure.
recommendations.change: Add H3s or a short FAQ phrased as queries: "Why isn't my contract visible in the ACE Platform UI or API?", "Can I use ACE with a vault, DEX, or lending protocol?", "Which contract types does ACE Beta support?" — answer each in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Agents retrieve by symptom/question string; the page holds these answers verbatim in body text but not in retrievable heading form.

recommendations.title: Add a summary limitations table
recommendations.issue: 0 tables; six distinct limitations are spread across prose sections.
recommendations.change: One table with columns Limitation · Beta status · Permanent vs. roadmap (e.g., "Custom extractors — not available — roadmap"; "Bring-your-own Data Validator — not offered — permanent by design").
recommendations.why: Tables are high-lift for extraction and let an engine distinguish temporary Beta gaps from permanent design choices — a distinction the page makes but buries.

recommendations.title: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with canonical URL and dates
recommendations.issue: Facts show 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`.
recommendations.change: Add `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-07-17`, `inLanguage`, and a `canonical` link mirroring the visible "Last Updated" body value.
recommendations.why: Structured freshness and canonical signals raise agent trust and dedupe; the freshness data already exists in body and just needs machine exposure.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with specifics
recommendations.where: "Additional networks may be added"; "PII are used"; general "some/most" usage.
recommendations.change: Where a count or list exists, state it (e.g., number of supported networks, or link count). Fix "PII are used" → "PII is used."
recommendations.why: Quantified claims outperform qualitative prose in citation rate.

recommendations.title: Attach units to bare numerals
recommendations.where: "Ten addresses per evaluation", "One active policy per organization".
recommendations.change: Phrase as explicit limits: "Max 10 unique wallet addresses per workflow execution"; "Limit: 1 active offchain policy per organization."
recommendations.why: Unit-bearing limits are precisely the quantitative specifics engines lift into answers.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal `wallet_risk_scoring` config snippet
recommendations.where: "Managed offchain risk policies are limited during Beta"
recommendations.issue: Feature described in prose only; agents integrating it have no copy-pasteable anchor.
recommendations.change: Add a short fenced, language-tagged example showing the policy declaration and the TRM credential reference.
recommendations.why: Runnable, labeled snippets raise agent task-completion and citation likelihood.

antiPatterns: Grammar slip: "no personally identifiable information (PII) are used."
No stale-content or dangling-cross-reference issues; "below" links resolve to real anchors.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced from the page — good site-level signal; verify it lists this URL.
JSON-LD/canonical are template-level; a fix here should propagate across `/ace/*`.
CLI should pass raw `<head>` on future runs — head metadata could not be verified, so the metadata score reflects served HTML only.
